questions.q: In this capstone's six-stage pipeline, which stages are built before any of the three front-end tools are touched?
options: None — all three front-ends are built in parallel with the warehouse
Only the Power BI stage, since it's considered the primary deliverable
The warehouse (dw.* schema) and the Python validation layer
Only the source AdventureWorks2012 tables, which already exist
questions.explain: The warehouse and its validation layer are stages 2 and 3, built and proven correct before Power BI, Tableau, or Excel work begins.

questions.q: What is the grain of dw.FactProductSales?
options: One row per customer
One row per order line (one row per Sales.SalesOrderDetail record)
One row per product category
One row per quarter
questions.explain: The fact table's grain is one row per order line — every column added to it has to be true at that grain.

questions.q: Why does dw.DimProduct flatten category and subcategory directly onto it instead of using separate dimension tables for them?
options: Because AdventureWorks2012 doesn't have category or subcategory tables
To give report builders one simple product dimension with category/subcategory already resolved, instead of three separate joined tables
Because Power BI cannot handle more than one dimension table
Because flattening is required by Tableau's connector
questions.explain: Flattening category and subcategory onto DimProduct via the join at build time means every front-end gets one simple dimension table instead of re-joining three tables itself.

questions.q: Why does the Python validation layer sit between the warehouse and the front-ends, rather than being a one-time manual check?
options: Because the warehouse refreshes on a schedule, and nobody can manually re-verify it every night before three front-ends trust it
Because Python is required by Microsoft SQL Server licensing
Because Tableau cannot connect directly to SQL Server without it
Because it replaces the need for a warehouse entirely
questions.explain: An automated script is the only realistic way three independent front-ends can all trust the same nightly-refreshed warehouse without re-verifying it themselves.

questions.q: What does "read-only consumer" mean in this architecture, and which deliverable is explicitly NOT allowed to break that rule?
options: It means a front-end only queries the warehouse and never writes back to it — even Finance, once they find a discrepancy later in this capstone, fixes it in their own workbook, not in the warehouse
It means only Power BI is allowed to query the warehouse
It means the warehouse is read-only and can never be refreshed
It means Tableau Public visitors can edit the underlying data
questions.explain: Each front-end, including Finance's Excel workbook, is a read-only consumer of the warehouse. When a discrepancy is found later, the fix happens in the consuming tool, not by writing back into dw.*.
